criteria.criterion: An ACLI failure whose stderr carries an authentication/authorization marker is detected from stderr, not from a subprocess exit code of 401 that ACLI never returns. Unit test asserts a CalledProcessError with returncode=1 + that stderr is recognised as an auth failure.

Such a failure aborts on the first attempt without consuming the retry budget — retrying a rejected credential is deterministic and cannot succeed. Unit test asserts the subprocess was invoked exactly once (today: 3 times).
The failure raises a distinct typed error (not a bare CalledProcessError) carrying the failing command, so callers can except it specifically. Unit test asserts the type.

A pass failing this way emits an operator-facing message that names the credential as the cause, distinguishable from the generic reconcile_once raised: ... used for data/operational failures. Unit test asserts the classifier's message/disposition.
Non-auth ACLI failures keep their existing retry-and-backoff behaviour unchanged. Regression test asserts a non-auth non-zero exit still makes 3 attempts.
